baseline.note: CLEAN run, F81. No DSV4_DPROF, no DSV4_KSWEEP, no TCB_CPA; NDEC=8, NGEN0=24 (9 verifies), block=5, passes=1, adaptK=1.50, prompt 0; clocks pinned, caches dropped. GATE PASS, MATCH 5/5, LOSSLESS GATE PASS, first token 11111, acceptance 2.89 unchanged. NOT A GAIN: F81's lever ships default OFF and this run measures the IDENTICAL default arm as clean_post_f79.log, which is the point of it -- the spec token sequence is BYTE-IDENTICAL to that log and ptxas -v shows the shipped smemB_kernel<8,2,false> unchanged at 64 registers / 0 spill / 17408 B. THIS IS THE SECOND IDENTICAL-ARM CLEAN PAIR AND IT RE-PRICES TRAP 25. The nine verifies pair 1:1 at identical K and identical accept counts for 1194.7 -> 1196.7 ms = +0.17%, only 2 of 9 in one direction, per-verify +1.21/-0.09/-0.15/+0.17/+0.28/+0.16/+0.00/+0.13/+0.00%; spec 22.07 -> 22.06 (-0.05%), base 13.78 -> 13.83 (+0.36%). Trap 25's ~1.5% floor came from ONE pair (f76->f79, 9/9 in one direction). With two pairs the reading changes: the instrument is capable of ~0.2% reproducibility and the 1.5% was an OCCASIONAL SYSTEMATIC SHIFT, not a per-run noise band. So a SINGLE cross-run claim under ~1.5% is still unsupportable (you cannot tell which pair you drew), but a sub-1% effect IS resolvable with TWO pairs -- which matters because everything left in LEVERS.md section 4 is sub-1%.

queue.what: cp.async/TMA staging global->shared for the fp8 tile with a >=4-stage smem ring. BUILT and RETIRED. Bit-exact (gate_tc_fp8_kc 1512/1512). Passed BOTH cheap steps: sm_110a assembles cp.async.bulk.tensor/mbarrier, and ptxas -v gave 48 regs / 36864 B / 5 blocks-per-SM against the shipped smemB<8,2,false>'s 64 / 17408 / 4 -- 16 registers handed back and occupancy UP 25%, the exact bar F78 failed. Then gemm_bench COLD at M=5 vs m16+smem B+4: wq_a +23.9%, wq_b +38.4%, wkv +52.8%, wo_b +39.9%, sw1/3 +14.9%, sw2 +36.3%. NS=2 beats NS=4 on 4 of 6 shapes, so DEPTH IS NEGATIVE -- the direct refutation of the promoted claim. Re-benched at B+0 for cp-size 16 (the engine's weights are 4-byte aligned, F66, so the ring is forced to cp-size 4): recovers ~25% and STILL loses at 5 of 6 shapes (+5.7/+11.7/+11.1/+26.4/+19.6%, sw1/3 -3.0%), so no alignment work rescues it. Not run in situ: falsification order says stop at the first no, and the bench has never flipped sign on this kernel. Default OFF behind TCB_CPA.
queue.expected: was ~1-3%; MEASURED +15 to +53% SLOWER (+2 to +26% at ideal alignment)
queue.falsify: Executed in the stated order and it failed at step (3). Mechanism, new trap 29: one ring stage is ONE K-block, so wait_group+__syncthreads runs once per K-block where the shipped KC=2 pays it once per two -- and F74's ADOPTED win was raising bytes-per-barrier (-28.6% on q:wq_b). The ring moved the one thing that pays, backwards. Trap 30: the occupancy win (4 -> 5 blocks/SM) was real and did not help, because the kernel already runs wo_b at 199 of 233-240 GB/s. Trap 31: cp-size 4 costs ~25% vs cp-size 16 and this engine's alignment forces it. REOPENING would need a design that does NOT lower bytes-per-barrier, which no cp.async ring at one K-block per stage can be.

queue.expected: 0.3-0.5% -- SUB-1%, does not count toward the pivot queue

queue.what: suffix-automaton / prompt-lookup drafting ahead of the MTP. RETIRED: the ORACLE max(MTP,suffix) is +0.0%.
queue.falsify: Executed at its own falsification (price it as ACCEPTANCE, a counted integer, immune to the 1.5% floor). 21 verifies: MTP 61 tokens / 2.905 per verify; suffix-only 23 / 1.095 (-62.3%); oracle 61 = +0.0%; 0 wins, 17 losses; match existed in only 8/21 and mlen never reached the block size. Mechanism: the drafting anchor is ALWAYS the correction token -- the one the MTP just mispredicted -- so a retrieval drafter is selected to be queried at the least repetitive point in the sequence (mlen=0 in 13 of 21). Measured on a period-8 degenerate repeating decode, the best case such a drafter can be handed. REOPENING needs a long-repeated-context prompt (shape of scripts/prompt_suite.json longctx_001, ids from tools/encode_prompt.py) on which mlen routinely reaches the block size.

queue.what: FP4 for MLA/dense weights -- moves the byte floor ~1.2x but violates 'no additional quantisation'. Needs an explicit decision from the operator to relax the constraint.

The research branch ran for the FIRST TIME in cycle 15: 6 WebSearch queries, one per axis A-F, all appended to RESEARCH_LOG.md section 2 with outcomes including the four that found nothing. Promoted 1 (B8-cpasync); folded UniSpec's n-gram confidence estimator into S6 as its gating rule, now moot since S6 is retired. M=5 vs m16+smem B+4: wq_a 0.0402->0.0498 (+23.9%), wq_b 0.0307->0.0425 (+38.4%), wkv 0.0269->0.0411 (+52.8%), wo_b 0.1066->0.1491 (+39.9%), sw1/3 0.0570->0.0655 (+14.9%), sw2 0.0562->0.0766 (+36.3%). measured.alignment_disambiguation: The engine's fp8 weights are 4-byte aligned (F66: 43470/44436 at offset%16==8, 966 at 12, none at 0), so cp.async is forced to cp-size 4. Re-benched at B+0 for cp-size 16: recovers ~25% (wo_b 0.1428 -> 0.1067) and STILL loses at 5 of 6 shapes vs m16+smem at the same B+0 -- wq_a +5.7%, wq_b +11.7%, wkv +11.1%, wo_b +26.4%, sw2 +19.6%, sw1/3 -3.0%. NO ALIGNMENT WORK RESCUES IT, which is what makes this a permanent close instead of a block on F67's shard pad.

Nine verifies pair 1:1 at identical K and accept counts: 1194.7 -> 1196.7 ms = +0.17%, only 2 of 9 in one direction, spec 22.07 -> 22.06 (-0.05%), base 13.78 -> 13.83 (+0.36%). negative_results: THE LEVER, and it failed in the most informative way available: it WON both cheap proxies and lost the timing. 16 registers handed back, occupancy 4 -> 5 blocks/SM, more bytes in flight, bit-exact -- and 15-53% slower.

THE DEPTH AXIS. NS=2 beats NS=4 beats NS=8 on most shapes. The literature's '>=4 stages, because 2 stalls tensor-core issue almost immediately' is backwards on this kernel, and that sentence was the entire evidential basis for promoting the lever in cycle 15.
THE ALIGNMENT ESCAPE ROUTE, closed by measuring it rather than by argument. cp-size 4 costs ~25%, and cp-size 16 still loses at 5 of 6 shapes.

THE MECHANISM, and it is a standing constraint rather than a detail (new trap 29): on this tile the binding resource is BARRIERS PER BYTE. F74's adopted win was raising bytes-per-barrier (KC K-blocks per barrier pair, -28.6% on q:wq_b); a ring at one K-block per stage halves it again. A stage is 8 KB over 256 threads -- too little work to amortise a wait_group plus a __syncthreads.

AN OCCUPANCY WIN THAT IS WORTH NOTHING (new trap 30). Trap 21 taught that losing 4 registers can cost 25% of occupancy; F81 is the converse and it does not hold -- the kernel already runs wo_b at 199 of 233-240 GB/s, so the 5th block adds contention, not bandwidth.
controls: Default-OFF is PROVEN, not asserted: byte-identical spec token sequence vs clean_post_f79.log, acceptance 2.89 unchanged, and ptxas -v confirming the shipped instantiation's register/smem/spill numbers are unmoved.
The bench has a within-bench control: at M=1 the dispatcher uses the m1 GEMV, so the cpa columns must equal their neighbours, and they do.
Arms placed at ADJACENT sweep positions (trap 5), and the alignment arm compared against the m16+smem column at the SAME B offset rather than across offsets.
gate_tc_fp8_kc sweeps a ring depth larger than KB, so the empty-commit_group padding that keeps wait_group at a compile-time depth cannot pass by never being exercised (trap 9).

counter_note: consecutive_sub_half_pct 4 -> 5. open_nontraining_levers 1 -> 0, and this is the FIRST audit at 0, so the queue-empty arm of the pivot criterion needs one more. It does not matter: the three-cycles-without-a-1%-adoption arm FIRED at cycle 14 and this is the fifth such cycle. What cycles 15 and 16 add is that both items the cycle-14 pivot analysis named as remaining have now been MEASURED dead rather than projected dead -- S6 at an oracle ceiling of exactly +0.0% (F80) and B8-cpasync at +15 to +53% in a COLD bench (F81). Counted honestly the kernel queue is empty: B8'' (~0.4%) and B1 (0.3-0.5%) are sub-1%, B5 needs the no-additional-quantisation constraint relaxed, S5 and S7 need training, B9 is prefill not decode, S3 is priced and rejected on arithmetic, S2 and S4 have no number. S5 is the only lever left with an unmeasured upside.
note_for_executor: YOU CANNOT RUN GIT -- write .flywheel_commit_msg and stop. Read LEVERS.md and RESEARCH_LOG.md first. THREE NEW RULES FROM F81: (1) A CHEAP PROXY THAT SAYS GO IS NOT A RESULT. ptxas -v said 48 registers vs 64 and 5 blocks/SM vs 4 -- the exact bar F78 failed -- and the kernel was still 15-53% slower. Occupancy and bytes-in-flight are means; time is the result (traps 29, 30). (2) BEFORE ADDING PIPELINE DEPTH, CHECK WHICH DIRECTION THE LAST ADOPTED WIN MOVED. F74 was adopted for raising bytes-per-barrier; the ring lowered it, and that alone predicted the sign. (3) MEASURE THE CONFOUND WHILE THE HARNESS IS WARM. Benching cp-size 16 as well as cp-size 4 cost one bench run and no checkpoint, and it is the difference between 'blocked on alignment' (which invites a cycle spent on F67's shard pad) and a permanent close. STILL TRUE FROM F80: prefer a ceiling to a point estimate, and price as a counted integer where you can. STILL TRUE FROM F79/F80: do not pass one argument to every gate binary -- gate_encoding takes NONE, and that artefact has now recurred four times.

pivot_criterion.why: S5 (draft-head re-alignment) is a TRAINING job the autonomous loop cannot do. Kernel work and training compete for the same operator attention, so the loop must say plainly when kernel work has stopped paying rather than grinding sub-1% levers forever.
pivot_criterion.trigger: PIVOT when open_nontraining_levers == 0 on TWO consecutive audits, OR when three consecutive cycles adopt nothing >=1%. Either fires -> the auditor writes a PIVOT banner to FLYWHEEL_AUDIT.md and creates FLYWHEEL_PIVOT.
pivot_criterion.note: ZERO, counted honestly, and this is the FIRST audit at 0 -- the queue-empty arm needs a second consecutive one. B8-cpasync was the sole occupant and F81 retired it with a bench number (+15 to +53%, and +2 to +26% even at the 16-byte alignment the engine does not have). Nothing was promoted to replace it: this cycle's measurement closed the fp8 GEMM block in every remaining direction rather than opening anything. B8'' (~0.4%) and B1 (0.3-0.5%) are explicitly sub-1% and do NOT count. S5 and S7 need training. B5 needs the no-additional-quantisation constraint relaxed. B9 is prefill, not decode. S3 is priced and rejected. S2 and S4 have never been priced with a number. The OTHER arm of the trigger -- three consecutive cycles adopting nothing >=1% -- has been fired since cycle 14 and this is the fifth, so the pivot is due now regardless of the count.

position_at_definition.reading: The remaining kernel headroom is ~30% and is spread across many sub-1% items; the acceptance multiplier alone is worth 1.4x. When the kernel queue empties, the pivot is not a defeat -- it is the point where the larger lever becomes the only lever.
